related_questions.question: What medicine should I take for COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: For most people with mild COVID-19, over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil) can help manage symptoms. However, if you have underlying health conditions, are over 65, or are immunocompromised, prescription medications like antivirals may be recommended to reduce the severity and duration of the illness. It's crucial to consult with a healthcare professional to determine the most appropriate treatment for your specific situation, especially if you have any concerns or risk factors.

list.title: Over-the-counter medications:
list.snippet: These can help with symptoms like fever, aches, and pains.

list.title: Prescription antivirals:
list.snippet: Medications like Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir and ritonavir) are available for those at higher risk of severe illness. These are most effective when started soon after symptom onset.

list.title: Consult a healthcare professional:
list.snippet: It's essential to talk to a doctor or other qualified healthcare provider to discuss your specific case and determine the best course of treatment. They can assess your risk factors, review your current medications to check for interactions, and prescribe the most appropriate medication.

list.title: Early treatment is key:
list.snippet: Don't delay seeking medical advice if you have symptoms of COVID-19. Early treatment can help prevent the illness from worsening.
